newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open firmer on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open firmer on technical rebound.

text.p: Singapore shares opened firmer early Friday on a technical rebound, dealers said.
"Blue chips have been consistently sold down. We are now just temporarily buying back," a foreign brokerage dealer said.
He said the downtrend was still intact with investors on the lookout to sell into strength.
At 0215 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) rose 12.21 points to 1,974.61.
Aiding the index was a recovery in stocks like motor-based Cycle & Carriage at Singapore S$14.60, up Singapore 20 cents.
Food companies like Fraser & Neave rose to S$10.10, up 20 cents and Cerebos Pacific was unchanged at S$5.85 after Thursday's sell-off due to its exposure in Thailand.
But overall volume was thin at 30 million shares.
Dealers cited the overnight surge in the Dow Jones Industrial Average to a record of 7,895.81, up 100.43 points, as another factor bolstering the early market.
Small issues keep their top positions in the actives list headed by auto parts distributor Tye Soon, which hit a new high of S$0.585 and was later at S$0.565, up half a cent.
Liquid crystal products maker IDT also peaked at a new high of US$1.17, and steadied at US$1.14 up five cents.
Dealers said small stocks and U.S. dollar issues were in favour, fuelled by a mixture of punting interest and dollar strength.
